mainTopic: Settling רבי יוחנן's view on lower-quality ביכורים, the story of עפריים, and a new משנה on growing and checking the best grain for מנחות
overview: The גמרא first asks how רבי יוחנן fits with a ברייתא that seems to go against him. It answers that this is a dispute among תנאים, and רבי יוחנן follows the other side. It then returns to the משנה's rule that מנחות come only from the best produce, and tells a short story in which פרעה's magicians mock משה with a saying about עפריים, a town famous for its grain. A new משנה follows. It says grain for מנחות should not come from fertilized, irrigated, or tree-filled fields, though after the fact it is כשר. It also explains how to grow top-quality grain, and how the גזבר checks the flour for powder and worms. The גמרא asks whether the farmer plows again in the second year, and brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי that says 'חורש ושונה'. It then pushes back on that proof, since the משנה never mentions plowing twice. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How does רבי יוחנן fit the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the ברייתא seems to go against his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוחנן, there is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just shown that the ברייתות fit ריש לקיש. Now it asks: what about רבי יוחנן, whose view seems to clash with one of them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that lower-quality produce cannot be consecrated as ביכורים. One of the ברייתות discussed earlier seems to allow it, so his view looks contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; a problem with a view
But; here it turns to the other side of the dispute

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
phrases.notes: He is the one who said lower-quality produce cannot become ביכורים.

phrases.english: it is difficult?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from ריש לקיש, whose view was just reconciled, to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that lower-quality produce cannot be consecrated as ביכורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא appears to allow consecrating lower-quality produce, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: It is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים disagree, and brings another ברייתא that fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among תנאים, as it is taught: produce that grew on a roof or in a ruin, one brings it and recites. Produce that grew in a flowerpot or on a ship, one does not bring it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן does not need to fit every ברייתא. Other תנאים disagree, and he can follow them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is stricter: produce from a flowerpot or a ship is not brought at all. That shows there is a view among the תנאים that fits רבי יוחנן, so the earlier ברייתא is just the other side of the debate.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
A ruin; a destroyed building
A flowerpot or planter
He brings the ביכורים and recites the פסוקים that go with them
At all

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא that clashes with an אמורא is not always a refutation. The אמורא can follow a different תנא.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im, as it is taught:
Produce that grew on a roof or that grew in a ruin –
he brings it and recites,
phrases.notes: Recites means saying the פסוקים of ביכורים, דברים 26:5–10.

phrases.english: that grew in a flowerpot or that grew on a ship –
he does not bring it at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the אמורא follows a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects one side of a dispute among תנאים. רבי יוחנן follows the stricter side, shown in this other ברייתא.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: only the best produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that all מנחות come only from the choicest produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and all of them come only from the choicest produce, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote the משנה. It is setting up a comment about one of the places the משנה names, עפריים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the best places for grain, and עפריים was one of them. Quoting this line opens the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The choicest; the best quality
And so on; the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: And all of them come
phrases.notes: All of them means all the מנחות.

phrases.english: only from the choicest, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה went on to name the best places for grain, including עפריים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן אֵינָן בָּאוֹת אֶלָּא מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ביכורים discussion and returns to the משנה about מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחות are brought only from the best produce.

steps.title: יוחנא and ממרא mock משה
steps.stepSummary: פרעה's magicians mock משה for doing wonders in מצרים, the land of magic.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוחנא and ממרא said to משה: You are bringing straw to עפריים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show how famous עפריים was for its grain. פרעה's magicians mock משה with a saying that uses עפריים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing straw to a place full of grain is pointless. In the same way, they said, showing magic in מצרים, the center of magic, impresses no one.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw
Bringing in
A town famous for excellent grain

phrases.english: Yoḥana and Mamre said to Moses:
phrases.notes: These were פרעה's magicians, who copied the staff turning into a snake (שמות 7:10–12).

phrases.english: Are you bringing straw to Afarayim?!
phrases.notes: In other words, why bring something to a place already full of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the fame of עפריים, which the משנה mentioned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doing wonders in the land of magic is as pointless as bringing straw to a town full of grain.

steps.title: משה answers: bring vegetables to a vegetable town
steps.stepSummary: משה answers with a popular saying: bring your goods where people know their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: people say, "To a town of vegetables, carry vegetables."
steps.whatsHappening: משה answers the mockery with a common saying. His point is that a wonder means the most to people who are experts in that field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller brings vegetables to a vegetable town because the buyers there can tell good produce from bad. Likewise, the magic experts of מצרים are exactly the ones who will see that משה's wonders are real and far greater than theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: People say; introduces a popular saying
A town
Vegetables or greens
Take; carry

phrases.english: He said to them:
People say:
"To a town of vegetables, carry vegetables."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה's reply to the magicians' mockery.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A wonder is best shown where the experts can recognize how great it is.

steps.title: New משנה: fields that should not supply grain for מנחות
steps.stepSummary: Grain for מנחות should not come from fertilized, irrigated, or tree-filled fields, but if it does, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not bring grain from a fertilized field, an irrigated field, or a field of trees. But if one did bring it, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists fields whose grain should not be used for מנחות, but says that after the fact the offering still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the rule that מנחות come from the best produce. Grain from these fields is not top quality, so we avoid it from the start, but using it does not disqualify the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A fertilized field
An irrigated field
A field planted with trees
If he brought it, it is valid after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels here. "One may not bring" is the ideal from the start, but "if he brought it, it is כשר" means the offering is still valid.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not bring grain from a fertilized field,
nor from an irrigated field,
nor from a field of trees,
but if he brought it, it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מְבִיאִין לֹא מִבֵּית הַזְּבָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that continues the theme of choosing the best grain for מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally, grain from fertilized, irrigated, or tree-filled fields is not used for מנחות, but after the fact it is כשר.

steps.title: How to grow the best grain for מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the farming method: plow in year one, then sow in year two, seventy days before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He plows the field in the first year. In the second year he sows it seventy days before פסח, and it produces a lot of fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rules about choice grain for מנחות. It now gives a practical farming method for growing grain that makes excellent flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said מנחות must come from the choicest produce. Now it explains how to actually grow such grain. The field is plowed in the first year and left unsown, and only in the second year is it planted at a set time before פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He plows it (breaks up the soil of the field)
He sows it (plants the seeds)
Fine flour, the kind used for מנחות
Abundant, a lot

phrases.english: How does he do it?
phrases.notes: He means: how does a farmer grow grain good enough for מנחות?

phrases.english: He plows it the first year,
and in the second year he sows it
seventy days before Passover,
and it produces a lot of fine flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's discussion of where the best grain comes from by explaining how to grow it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plow the field in the first year; sow it in the second year seventy days before פסח, which yields abundant fine flour.

steps.title: How the treasurer checks the flour
steps.stepSummary: The גזבר puts his hand into the flour; if powder sticks to it, the flour is not allowed until it is sifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does the גזבר check the flour? He puts his hand into it. If powder comes up on his hand, it is not allowed until he sifts it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from growing the grain to checking the finished flour. It describes a simple hand test the Temple treasurer uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fine flour for מנחות must be clean of loose powder. If powder clings to the hand, the flour is still פסולה. But this is fixable: once it is sifted well, it becomes usable.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple treasurer, who was in charge of buying and checking supplies
Dust or fine powder
Unfit, not allowed to be used
He sifts it

steps.confusionAlert: This flour is not ruined forever. It is פסולה only until it is sifted, and then it may be used.

phrases.english: How does the treasurer check it?
He puts his hand into it.
If powder came up on it, it is unfit,
phrases.notes: "On it" means on his hand: when he pulls his hand out, powder is stuck to it.

phrases.english: until he sifts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from growing the grain to inspecting the flour made from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flour that leaves powder on the inspecting hand is unfit until it is sifted.

steps.title: Wormy flour is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: If the flour has worms, it is unfit for a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it became wormy, it is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one last rule about checking the flour: wormy flour may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the powder case, the משנה does not say "until" anything here. It simply says wormy flour is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: It became wormy (worms got into it)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rules for מנחה flour: grow it in a special way, check it by hand for powder (fixable by sifting), and do not use it if it is wormy.

phrases.english: And if it became wormy, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second way flour can fail inspection, after the powder test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wormy flour is unfit for a מנחה.

steps.title: Does the farmer plow again in the second year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's farming rule and asks whether, in year two, the farmer plows and sows, or only sows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said, "How does he do it? He plows it the first year." A question was asked: What does it mean? Does he plow in the first year, and in the second year plow and sow? Or maybe he plows in the first year, and in the second year sows without plowing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה's line about plowing. It then asks what the farmer does in the second year, because the משנה only says "he sows it."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions plowing in year one and sowing in year two, but does not say whether the field is plowed again in year two. There are two possible readings: plow again and then sow, or just sow on the field already plowed. The גמרא lays out both options and is setting up an answer that will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, an open question the Sages were unsure about
What is he saying? How should we read the words?
Or perhaps, introducing the second possibility
Without

phrases.english: GEMARA: How does he do it?
He plows it the first year.
A question was raised before them: What is it saying?
He plows it the first year
and the second year he plows it and sows it,
or perhaps he plows it the first year
and the second year he sows it without plowing it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts its discussion by going back to the משנה's farming rule from step 7 and asking what it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה means the field is plowed again in the second year before sowing, or sown without a second plowing.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the best fields for the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי. It says the עומר comes only from sunny southern fields that were plowed for this purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי יוסי says: even the grain of כרזיים and כפר אחים would have been brought for the עומר if those places were close to ירושלים. The עומר is brought only from southern fields that were plowed for this, because the sun shines on them all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof to answer the question from step 10. It opens with a ברייתא about which fields produce the best grain for the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opening part of the ברייתא does not answer the question yet. It sets the scene: the best fields get full sun and are plowed specially. The farming details that settle the question come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
Southern fields, facing the sun
Fields plowed and left open for this purpose
If only

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Also the grain of Kerazayim and Kefar Achim,
if only they were close to Jerusalem,
they would have brought from them,
because one does not bring the omer
except from the southern fields
and those plowed for this purpose,
for on them the sun rises,
and from them the sun sets.
phrases.notes: These fields get sun all day long, from sunrise to sunset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof that answers the question raised in step 10
steps.raayaObject: Whether in the second year the farmer plows and sows, or only sows
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי about growing the עומר grain

steps.title: The farming method: plow, plow again, then sow
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes the method: plow in year one, and in year two plow twice, then sow seventy days before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He plows the first year. In the second year he plows and plows again, and sows seventy days before פסח, so it is close to the sun. It grows a stalk one handspan long and an ear two handspans long.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the step-by-step farming method. This is the part that holds the answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ושניה חורש ושונה' say that in the second year the farmer plows, and plows again, before sowing. Our משנה only said 'sow' for year two, so it was unclear if plowing happens too. This ברייתא spells it out.

keyTerms.meaning: He plows it (breaks up the ground)
He plows and repeats the plowing
A handspan
The ear of grain, where the kernels are
The stalk

steps.whyThisMatters: This one phrase, חורש ושונה, is what the גמרא will point to in order to settle the question.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He plows it the first year,
and in the second, he plows and repeats,
and sows it seventy days before Pesach,
so that it will be close to the sun,
and it produces a stalk of a handspan
and an ear of two handspans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and reaches the part that matters for the proof
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is plowing in the second year
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'ושניה חורש ושונה' in the ברייתא

steps.title: Processing the grain and checking the flour
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the steps from harvest to flour, and how the treasurer checks it. רבי נתן adds that he oils his hand first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reaps, gathers, threshes, winnows, sorts, grinds and sifts, and brings it to the גזבר. The גזבר puts his hand in. If powder sticks to it, he says: 'Go back and sift it again.' In the name of רבי נתן they said: the גזבר smears his hand with oil and puts it in, so that all the powder comes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which goes on to describe making the flour and checking it. This part is not needed for the proof; it is quoted so the ברייתא is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain check is whether powder sticks to a dry hand. רבי נתן's check is stricter: an oiled hand picks up even a little powder, so the flour must be very clean to pass.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathers the cut grain into sheaves
Winnows, throwing the grain in the wind to remove chaff
Sifts the flour
Fine powder or dust in the flour
Smears or anoints

phrases.english: And he reaps and gathers it into sheaves,
and threshes, and winnows, and sorts,
and grinds, and sifts,
and brings it to the treasurer,
and the treasurer puts his hand into it.
If powder came up on it,
he says to him: "Go back and sift it a second time."
In the name of Rabbi Natan they said:
the treasurer smears his hand with oil,
and puts it into it
until he brings up all its powder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא; it matches what the משנה said in step 8
steps.raayaSupportSource: End of the ברייתא of רבי יוסי

steps.title: The proof: in year two he plows again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the words 'חורש ושונה' and concludes that in the second year the field is plowed, then sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: 'he plows and repeats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks out the one phrase that answers the question from step 10. Since the ברייתא says 'חורש ושונה', there is plowing in the second year too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיהת tells us: forget the other details, this is the part we need. The question was whether year two means plowing and sowing, or only sowing. The ברייתא says he plows twice and then sows, so the proof argues for plowing and sowing. The next step challenges whether this ברייתא can explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (pointing to the part that matters)

steps.whatToRemember: This is the proof the גמרא offers for the question from step 10: the ברייתא says the farmer plows in the second year. The next step pushes back on using this ברייתא to explain the משנה.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches
"he plows and repeats."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 11-13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the farmer plow and sow in the second year, or only sow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He plows and sows; the ברייתא says he plows twice in the second year before sowing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof claims there is plowing in the second year, because the ברייתא says 'חורש ושונה'. The next step challenges whether this ברייתא can explain the משנה.

steps.title: The proof is pushed back: the משנה never mentions plowing twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. Even by your own reasoning, the משנה does not say 'שׁוֹנֶה' (plow again), so the ברייתא cannot simply be used to explain the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even by your own reasoning, our משנה does not say 'he repeats' the plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the proof it just brought from the ברייתא of רבי יוסי. It points out that the ברייתא and the משנה don't line up anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 14 used the ברייתא's words 'חורש ושונה' to show that in year two the field is plowed and then sown. But the ברייתא says to plow twice in year two, and the משנה says nothing about a second plowing. Since the two sources already differ on this detail, we can't assume the משנה agrees with the ברייתא on the question we asked.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: 'even if we follow your own logic'. It is used to turn the other side's argument against them.
It teaches. Here it refers to what the משנה actually says.
Repeats. Here it means plowing a second time.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the גמרא saying the field is not plowed in year two. It is only saying the ברייתא can't prove what the משנה means, because the two texts already differ about plowing twice.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: He means: even if we follow the logic you just used from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: our משנה does not teach "he repeats" the plowing,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא said to plow twice in year two (Step 12), but the משנה never says that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 14 by showing that the ברייתא and the משנה already differ about plowing twice in year two.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the use of רבי יוסי's ברייתא to settle what the משנה means. It does not reject the ברייתא's own ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה follows the ברייתא. But the ברייתא requires plowing twice in year two ('שׁוֹנֶה'), and the משנה does not mention this. So the two sources don't fully match, and one can't be used to explain the other.
